<description>
The C++ Core Guidelines recommend **establishing an error handling strategy early in a project's design** ([E.1](https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#re-design)). Under the presumption that "we are still early" and given the fact that there is lots of development (eg #34931, #35003, #34132, ...) without such a strategy, it might be the right time to come up with a design document.

I post this as a PR rather than an Issue, because it will simplify giving feedback on individual parts of the text.
</description>

[2026-10-08] c:6058577228 comment by stickies-v (member):
[quoted text omitted]

So what does that mean practically? If a function's input parameter is documented to be non-null, and the function recognizes it has received a null pointer, but it can handle the situation (e.g. by returning early, by shutting down gracefully, ...), then the "Proper Defect handling" rule does not force us to terminate? Practically speaking, in cases where we don't want to tighten the crash behaviour, that means we'd be loosening contracts (e.g. document nullptr as allowed) rather than changing termination behaviour? I.e. only assert where we really have no other option but to crash, or where crashing is fine?

Perhaps to approach it from a different angle: what is the problem that you're addressing with the "Proper Defect handling" rule? In the developer notes, for example, we often add a rationale, and I think that would be helpful here too.

[quoted text omitted]
I definitely wasn't arguing for that. My argument was that documented rules/guidelines need to represent developer consensus on where we want to go, which is lacking especially for the error propagation mechanism. I agree that this kind of documentation can help us make more progress in a good direction.

[quoted text omitted]
At first glance, that seems like a sensible approach for a narrowly scoped (and newly carved out/refactored) part of the codebase, though I haven't thought through all the trade-offs yet. Could we document that for this new library, and discuss it further in the relevant PRs or in a dedicated issue? I think the global scope of the proposal is the hard sell here.
</new_statements>
